text: Agreed to pace rolling rides with steady endurance effort on climbs rather than surging, guided by conversational breathing and comfortable cadence.
A final riser felt unusually hard, but the likely causes were a headwind and a long day on the athlete's feet rather than a negative fitness trend.
For exposed headwinds, agreed to use a lower position and move snacks earlier to preserve final-hour energy, while monitoring hands and shoulders as volume rises.
Mild leg heaviness on day two of back-to-back rides cleared after 20 minutes of easy spinning; plan remains unchanged, with the ride to be shortened if heaviness ever persists beyond 30 minutes.
For rides over two hours, agreed on one bottle per hour, food every 30 minutes, and a larger breakfast before sustained climbing; the routine will first be practiced on easy rides.

Recovery spins will start from the park side of town because fewer junctions make it easier to maintain relaxed breathing and genuinely easy effort; these rides will be protected when scheduling gets busy.
